ambiguities.text: The specification does not define error responses for invalid requests
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard JSON-RPC error codes apply (e.g., -32602 for invalid params)

ambiguities.text: The meaning of 'whitelisted for that user' is not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume whitelisting is a per-dApp, per-user preference stored in the wallet for which assets to share

ambiguities.text: The 'types' filter mentions 'ERC20' and 'ERC721' but doesn't clarify handling of other standards
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume types is an extensible list and wallets should support known standards and return empty for unknown types

ambiguities.text: The specification doesn't specify if balances are returned at current block or a specific block number
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume balances are returned at the latest block unless the wallet provides block number metadata

implicit_assumptions.description: The wallet is trusted to accurately report asset ownership and balances
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious or buggy wallets could misrepresent user assets, leading to incorrect dApp behavior

implicit_assumptions.description: dApps use the justification parameter honestly to explain why they need asset data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users could be deceived into sharing asset information for unintended purposes

implicit_assumptions.description: Users understand the implications of sharing asset information with dApps
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users could unknowingly expose their financial portfolio to malicious applications

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot spoof the requesting dApp's identity to gain unauthorized asset information
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Phishing attacks could harvest user portfolio data by impersonating legitimate dApps
